options: It lets the current pass, so the circuit is complete
It makes the current, so the bulb lights

A switch does not store current.
A closed switch lets the current through.

solution: A closed switch completes the path.

The pencil lead made its own electricity
The bulb would have lit without the lead
Graphite is an insulator because it is not a metal

explain.why: The battery is the energy source.
The gap was open until the lead was added.
The bulb lit, so it conducts.

solution: The bulb lit, so graphite lets current pass.

It becomes larger because one bulb is removed

Q's path is still complete.
One path less means less current from the battery.

solution: Only one path is left, so less current flows from the battery.

The coin works only when taped

The bulb did not light through the tape.

The loop is still complete through the wire.

questions.stem: Which circuit part changes electrical energy into light and heat?

explain.why: A switch only opens and closes the circuit.
A battery provides the electrical energy.
A wire carries current.

solution: The bulb gives out light and heat.

questions.stem: In which situation will the bulb light up?
options: Two wires join the bulb to both ends of the battery
A wire joins only one end of the battery to the bulb
Two wires join the two ends of the battery together, with no bulb
The bulb is placed next to the battery without wires

explain.why: There is no complete path.
There is no bulb in the path.
There is no path between them.

solution: The bulb needs a complete path from one end of the battery to the other.

questions.stem: A student has a battery, a bulb, wires and these materials: iron key, plastic comb, glass marble, copper wire. Which two can be used to complete the circuit?

explain.why: Plastic is an insulator.
These are insulators.
Glass is an insulator.

solution: Metals conduct electricity.

questions.stem: In the circuit shown, S is closed but the bulb is not lit. A student replaces the battery with a new one and the bulb lights up. What was the problem?

explain.why: The same bulb lit with the new battery.
The switch is closed and was not changed.
The wires were not changed.

solution: Only the battery was changed, so it was the problem.
